profile_prompts.tool_execution: per turn: random token file planted in the session home; agent told to `cat <abs path>` and echo its output

method.cpu: per-turn process-tree CPU delta (see cpu_method in measurements); replaces HRS-005's cumulative RUSAGE_CHILDREN max() which misattributed CPU under concurrency
method.wall: duration_seconds = batch elapsed monotonic wall clock; per-turn walls kept for latency percentiles only
method.rss: rss_mb_peak = max tree tick sum; rss_mb_end = final tree sample of the last-finishing turn (HRS-005 wrongly published peak as end)
method.storage: du-equivalent byte sum over each session HERMES_HOME tree before/after the batch (sqlite_persistence only)
method.continuing_semantics: continuing = every turn after the first resumes the SAME session: preferred via `--resume <session-id>` (id read from the home's session store right after turn 0), fallback via bare `-c` (MRU inside the turn's isolated HERMES_HOME); explicit ids are preferred because the pin writes last_activity_at at process exit and that write is occasionally lost under load, which empties the MRU lookup while session content stays intact (observed live, c4). Continuation itself is VERIFIED per turn by codeword recall, not assumed
method.null_contract: every null is {value: null, reason: ...} or carries a sibling <field>_reason key (DF-HRS-102)

notes: Measured against the pinned Python reference via its real agent loop; provider/network latency is included (end-to-end, not compute-only). Local compute/resource measurement ONLY - this record makes no Python-vs-Rust compatibility or efficiency claim.

concurrency_math_check.assertion: duration_seconds in every rep file is the time.monotonic elapsed around the whole concurrent batch, never the sum of per-turn walls; wall_sum_over_batch >> 1 at concurrency>1 demonstrates the old summed-wall figure would have been wrong
